title_zh: 神通过IMB在意大利的传教士保持忠诚
content: The eastern face of St. Peter's Basilica in the Vatican City in Rome, Italy, is famous for its central balcony from which popes give their papal addresses. Most people in Rome have at least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” IMB Photo In the city where Jason and Lizzy Davis serve, some steps have a lot of meaning. And the meaning is different for them than it is for the thousands who travel there to visit that site. “If you come to Rome, you can come to a place called the Holy Steps,” Jason said. “People go there, and they’ll crawl up on their knees and pray the rosary all the way up.” From the top of the steps, a mural depicting Jesus on the Cross looks down on those making the pilgrimage. For Jason and Lizzy, it’s a spiritual experience, a picture of a religion that asks people to earn their way to Jesus. “That’s really the opposite of what the gospel is. The gospel is Jesus saying, ‘No, you can’t do it . . . no matter how good you think you are,’” they said. Most people in Rome have at the very least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism, as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” Jason explained, “It’s where the Pope lives in the Vatican. It’s very much part of the religion and culture. It’s all intertwined here.” An ‘unavoidable’ call Jason and Lizzy are investing their lives as International Mission Board missionaries in Rome, Italy, to share the truth of the gospel. The Davises partner with national believers through a new church plant, and they’re seeking to plant more churches within the city. Lizzy said for her, the call to missions was unavoidable. “I grew up as a third culture kid, or a missionary kid. My parents were on the mission field, as were my grandparents, all with the International Mission Board.” Then her family moved to Virginia for her dad to work for IMB’s home office staff. As a middle schooler and high schooler, every time Lizzy heard about the need for the gospel to go forth, she felt a burden, a “burning” in her heart. She didn’t know what God would do with that, but she had a feeling she would see one day. Now, years later, she and Jason spend their time trying to find as many opportunities as they can to invite people into their home so they can share the hope of Jesus with them. That can mean Bible study or simply sharing a meal. ‘Completely lost’ Jason has been surprised by just how often people are willing to talk about faith. “You can get into spiritual conversations very quickly with people, especially if you’re just open and honest with them.” Lizzy shared that one of the easiest ways to do this is to be willing to let your day be interrupted. “That’s something I’ve seen Jason do firsthand in our neighborhood. He walks down the street, and everybody knows him because he stops and takes the time to ask them questions about their families, gets to know people, gets to know the newspaper stand guy and the guy at the fruit stand and the grocery store ladies.” She emphasized that caring about people is “what Christ would do.” The Davises, whose previous mission service prevents their photos from being published, live in a neighborhood of about 130,000 people. Their church of 15 people is the only evangelical congregation there. Lizzy said the area is “truly a lost, completely lost, dark neighborhood” with people who have never heard the gospel. Thousands more come to their area on a religious quest. The Davis family’s neighborhood is home to the Basilica Papale di San Paolo (the Papal Basilica of Saint Paul), one of the city’s four major basilicas. “So we get a lot of people coming on spiritual journeys, visiting our neighborhood, seeking some sort of spiritual experience. And oftentimes it’s just trying to earn their salvation,” she added. Jason described this environment as “a genuine need for people to actually hear the gospel and know that their sins can be forgiven and they can have an assurance of that.” IMB missionaries Jason and Liz

content: Rebeca Couto, a global missionary partner from the Azores islands, practices writing characters with her tutor in Japan. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto poses with her violin. Couto is a professional violinist who is serving as a global missionary partner with the IMB in Japan. Doors have opened for her to use her skills with evangel ical Japanese musicians who perform. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto moved from one volcanic archipelago to another, leaving Portugal’s Azores islands to anchor her life in Japan. The percentage of evangelical Christians in the Azores and Japan is similar, with both populations under 1%. Couto is a fourth-generation Christian, a rarity on the small islands. She is one of few, if any, believers in the Azores with such a long spiritual lineage. This rich legacy shaped her and prepared her for ministry. “I’ve always understood the Great Commission as a call for all believers and all disciples of Christ to be missionaries, wherever they are, whatever they’re doing, and whatever God has equipped them with,” Couto said. Couto’s great-grandfather became a Christian through the witness of missionaries from the United Kingdom. Later, missionaries from the Foreign Mission Board, now the International Mission Board, started the first Baptist work in the Azores by planting an English-speaking church near an American military base. A Baptist Brazilian couple planted a Portuguese-speaking church, which became the congregation where Couto grew up and was commissioned as a missionary. Ministry has been passed down through the generations of her family. Couto’s father has pastored for 20 years, and both of her parents have been involved in ministry for most of their lives. Couto now serves in Japan as a global missionary partner, a missionary who is financially supported by a sending church or organization in their home country and serves with IMB teams. Close to 400 GMPs currently serve on IMB teams around the world. Language learning Couto is immersed in language study in Yokohama, Japan. She had a head start before she even arrived. After graduating from high school, Couto moved from the Azores to Lisbon to pursue a degree in music. She spent hours on public transportation and wanted a challenge to pass the time. She decided to study Japanese because she thought it sounded beautiful. At the time, she had no intention of becoming a missionary in the traditional sense. However, the more she learned about the language and the culture, her burden for the lost grew. She began researching Christianity in Japan. “I understood how bleak the scenario was, and how much the country needed Jesus. I struggled with that calling because the doors were closed, and it didn’t seem possible to come to Japan for a myriad of reasons,” Couto said. After finishing master’s degrees in music and violin performance, along with a seminary degree, Couto was considering pursuing a Ph.D. or returning to seminary when her seminary professors, IMB missionaries Jonathan and Bethany Sharp, contacted her about serving as a missionary in Japan. They introduced her to the GMP program and invited her to attend a missions immersion school they piloted . Music to their ears As a professional violinist, Couto brought her violin to Japan, unsure of what opportunities existed, but she knew her call to the mission field somehow involved her gifting. “I see myself as having been called to serve through music. I never even conceived doing missions while excluding the violin entirely,” Couto said. She continued, “Music is such a universal way to connect with people, and it’s so intuitive to pair that with the gospel and with God’s message to people’s hearts.” While she knew the Lord would somehow open a door for her to use the violin for kingdom work, she was at peace with the possibility that, for a season, she may not be as active in music. That, however, was not the case. “I’ve always understood the Great Commission as a call for all believers and all disciples of Christ

title_zh: IMB传教士使用家庭、咖啡馆、应用程序为西班牙的福音对话敞开大门
content: Men and women gather to discuss spiritual topics with Caleb and Carina Beaty, International Mission Board missionaries who serve in Madrid. IMB Photo Across Spain, people looking for connection and meaningful conversation turn to the internet to find groups where they can meet others. At a café by the river, Caleb and Carina Beaty engage in conversations about finding purpose, beauty and “what’s wrong with the world.” A website called Meetup allows people to search for groups to meet in person. The description of the Beatys’ group indicates that it discusses spiritual topics. People come expecting to talk about faith, so it’s not a surprise when they arrive. Caleb said he always has a list of questions that begin broadly and funnel into questions such as, “If there were a God …” or “What do you think Christians believe about that?” or “Why do you think religions have such different perspectives?” The Beatys’ goal in these conversations is to work toward deeper worldview questions within 45 minutes to an hour. Most of the people who attend their Meetup group are from Madrid, but they also have conversations with people from other countries. During one Meetup, Caleb and Carina shared how creation was perfect, but sin led to a world separated from the Father. God offers salvation through the death and resurrection of Jesus, they explained. “There are times we’re able to get to a clear gospel presentation with a group of people, and sometimes we’re doing pre-evangelism.” Caleb said. Some repeat attendees who have been attending for more than a year quickly jump to the heart of the discussion. “All right, Caleb, what’s the Bible say about suffering?” they’ll ask. Caleb and Carina then have the opportunity to share the Christian perspective. IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty and their children pose for a photo in a park in Madrid, Spain.  IMB Photo Spain has secularized rapidly since the 1990s, Caleb said. While many may think of it as a Catholic nation, many people do not know the basic tenets of Christianity. “We’ve got all the churches, we’ve got the cathedrals, and they do processions, but the average person on the street does not know anything about the gospel and does not know anything about Jesus,” Caleb said. Younger Spaniards are drawn to their group and are receptive to the gospel because they don’t have a spiritual foundation or know anyone who does. “There’s just this curiosity because, for a lot of them, they’ve never met someone who actually believes that God exists, and that changes your life,” Carina said. “I’ve had people completely shocked that we believe in God. ‘You really believe that God exists?’ They can’t wrap their mind around that.” During one Meetup, a man contrasted Protestant and Catholic beliefs by saying Protestants focus on Jesus’ suffering and Catholics on Mary’s grief. Caleb responded that evangelicals focus on the resurrection. When Caleb said Jesus rose from the dead, the man replied that he needed to look into that. Caleb said encounters like that reveal how little many Spaniards know about the gospel. Caleb noted the irony of the man’s sharing the Catholic perspective without truly understanding it. He is not the only person the Beatys have met who has missed the heart of the gospel. A friend of the Beatys told them she’d heard Jesus died, but she hadn’t heard he rose from the dead. A man reads a passage of Scripture during a Bible study hosted by IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty at their family’s apartment in Madrid, Spain. Five atheists began attending their Bible study after attending the couple’s Meetup group. IMB Photo The Beatys also host seasonal outreach events through the Meetup. Members from their church in Madrid have started attending the Meetup to learn how the Beatys lead discussions. Their group has become so popular, a waitlist has formed. Caleb and Carina host a small-group Bible study in their home. Five atheists who joined their Meetup now attend the Bible study.

content: IMB Graphic NASHVILLE – As the books closed on the latest fiscal year, receipts for the two Southern Baptist national annual missions offerings underscored the value Southern Baptist churches place on reaching the world with the gospel. The Lottie Moon Christmas Offering® (LMCO) totaled $212.5 million to support International Mission Board (IMB) missionaries, and the Annie Armstrong Easter Offering® (AAEO) reached $73.6 million to support the North American Mission Board’s (NAMB) church planting, compassion ministry and other evangelistic efforts to reach North America. IMB President Paul Chitwood said he celebrates what God did in the 2025-26 season and what He is doing now to lead Southern Baptists toward historic generosity. “I thank God for Southern Baptists! With giving through the Lottie Moon offering at an all-time high, churches and individual givers continue to display a heart for the gospel to be proclaimed to every nation, all tribes, peoples and languages,” Chitwood said. The Annie total marked the second highest in NAMB’s history. The record Lottie Moon offering total surpassed last year’s total by more than $5 million and is the best offering in IMB history. “God is giving our generation unprecedented opportunity to send missionaries to the most unreached peoples and places,” Chitwood continued. “Though the challenges faced by our missionaries are enormous, the generosity of Southern Baptists ensures they have what they need to face those challenges and continue in the work while we hold the ropes with our support.” IMB missionary Landon Williams (center) walks with a Chilean pastor and a U.S. pastor on a remote island in Chile. Cooperation and generosity among Southern Baptists fuels the work to reach the uttermost parts of the world with the gospel. IMB Photo National goals for both offerings are set in partnership with Woman’s Missionary Union (WMU) each year. In response to the offering totals, Sandy Wisdom-Martin, executive director-treasurer of WMU, said: “As Southern Baptists, we are all in for His mission. When we give sacrificially, we prioritize the mission of God. Together our fervent prayers, our faithful generosity and our wholehearted obedience become channels for the gospel to reach our neighbors as well as the nations.” For the last 10 years, Southern Baptists have increasingly supported the Annie offering, setting records in seven of the last 10 years. Totals in each of the last four years have surpassed $70 million. “I am so grateful to the pastors and churches for the faithfulness and generosity they have demonstrated through this offering,” said NAMB president Kevin Ezell. “As I travel and speak in churches of all sizes, I love seeing the posters in the hallways showing their offering goals. For some it is a few hundred dollars, for others several thousand.” The Annie Armstrong offering supports more than 3,000 missionaries in North America, including the ongoing work of church planting in the U.S. and Canada. In 2025, Southern Baptists planted the largest number of churches, 699, since 2016. Including church plants and replants, Southern Baptists have surpassed 700 new churches in four of the last five years. More than 12,000 churches have been planted since 2010. To go along with the increased giving totals to the SBC’s missions offerings, Southern Baptists have also increased their local outreach efforts, indicating that the focus is not just on giving but on sending. Baptism totals have increased in each of the last five years, recovering from the pandemic-year low in 2020 to surpass the 2017 total. The five consecutive years of increase marked the first such streak in approximately 75 years. title: Oklahoma Baptists join Sending Church Lab to strengthen missionary support

title_zh: 俄克拉荷马州浸信会加入派遣教会实验室，以加强传教士支持
content: Staff members at First Baptist Church in Wagoner, Oklahoma, evaluate their church’s involvement with missions and missionary support. IMB Photo The chapel at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City turned into a science lab on Oct. 5-6. Microscopes, beakers and test tubes weren’t in the room, but this Sending Church Lab drew nearly 40 people representing 12 Oklahoma Baptist churches committed to send and care for international missionaries well. The Sending Church Lab, facilitated by the International Mission Board, brought pastors, church leaders and missionaries together for two days of discussion, self-assessment and planning centered on one question: What does it mean for a church to truly be a sending church? For Mike Wall, a global missions ministry partner of Oklahoma Baptists, the answer begins with churches reclaiming responsibility for the Great Commission. Wall first attended a Sending Church Lab last year in Tulsa with few expectations. He left convinced more churches needed the training. “When I went there, I thought, ‘You’ve got to do this in Oklahoma City,’” Wall said, “because of the content and how much our churches need something just like this.” After observing churches work through the exercises in the lab, Wall said he was encouraged by an emphasis on local church ownership in missions. “We can’t just send our people and say, ‘OK, now this is your job, IMB,’” he said. “We have to do our job in sending, preparing and training the best ‘sent ones’ so that when they get to the field, they can already hit the ground running.” Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement specialist, leads a Sending Church Lab at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City. He is emphasizing the importance of sending churches assessing and equipping future IMB missionaries. IMB Photo Leading the lab was Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement strategist, who developed the concept after seeing the need for stronger relationships between missionaries and local churches. “A Sending Church Lab is our attempt to raise up a host of IMB sending churches,” Wooten said, crediting the North American Mission Board for doing similar events and having successful results. The lab helps churches understand what Wooten calls the church engagement pathway: praying, cooperating, partnering and sending. While many churches faithfully pray, give and go, he said sending requires something more intentional. “Sending includes taking responsibility for an IMB missionary by providing ongoing encouragement, accountability and soul care throughout their term of service,” he explained. During the two-day event, participants gathered around whiteboards to evaluate their church’s missions practices, identify strengths and weaknesses and develop plans for improvement. “We don’t just need to deliver content,” Wooten said. “We need to invite churches to do some work on their own.” Rather than simply listening to presentations, attendees worked through practical questions about prayer, giving, short-term missions, missionary assessment and long-term care. Wooten said churches consistently tell him the greatest benefit is clarity. “They are thankful for clarity on what an IMB sending church is and what our roles and responsibilities are,” he said. For IMB missionaries Peter and Katie Weeks, that clarity is especially valuable. They participated in the lab alongside church leaders. Their real names have been changed to protect their work in Southeast Asia. “There’s no other place I’d rather be during these few days than here,” Peter said. Katie appreciated the interactive nature of the training. “I really appreciate the way they’re actually requiring information from the different churches and encouraging dialogue about how they can go through the steps,” she said. content_zh: 俄克拉何马州瓦戈纳第一浸信会的工作人员评价了教会参与传教和传教活动的情况。 IMB 相片 俄克拉荷马城Constitute Road Baptist Church的小教堂于10月5-6日变成科学实验室. 但这个送信教会实验室吸引了近40人, 代表12个俄克拉何马浸会教会, 传教士实验室在国际传教委员会的协助下,召集牧师、教会领袖和传教士进行两天的讨论、自我评估和规划,其中心是一个问题: 教会真正成为送教之所意味着什么? 对于俄克拉何马浸信会的全球使命部合作伙伴迈克·沃尔来说,答案始于教会重新为大委员会负责。 去年沃尔在图尔萨参加了一个送教实验室, 他离开后确信更多的教会需要训练. “当我去那里时,我想,`你必须在俄克拉荷马城做这件事,'墙说,`因为内容和我们的教会需要这样的东西。 在观察了教堂通过实验室的演练工作后,沃尔说,他在任务中强调当地教会的所有权使他受到鼓舞. “我们不能只是派我们的人来说,“好吧,这是你的工作,IMB。” “我们必须在派遣、准备和训练最优秀的`派遣 ' 人员方面完成我们的工作,这样,当他们到达实地时,他们就已经可以奔跑地了。” Bryan Wooten,IMB高级教会订婚专家,在俄克拉荷马城的Constitution Road Baptist教堂领导一个送教实验室. 他强调派遣教会评估和装备未来的IMB传教士的重要性. IMB Photo Leading the lab是IMB高级教会接触策略师布莱恩·伍滕(Bryan Wooten),他在看到传教士与本地教会之间需要更牢固的关系后发展出这个概念. 伍腾说,“一个派遣教会实验室是我们努力培养许多派遣教会的IMB。 ”他赞扬北美传教委员会开展了类似的活动并取得了成功。 实验室帮助教会理解伍腾所谓的教会参与途径:祈祷,合作,合作和发送. 虽然许多教堂忠实地祈祷,奉献和去,但他说送去需要更有意图的东西. 他解释说,“最后包括负责一个IMB传教士,在整个任职期间提供持续的鼓励、问责和精神关怀。” 在为期两天的活动期间,与会者聚集在白板周围,评价其教会的任务做法,查明优缺点并制订改进计划。 」伍腾说: “我们需要邀请教会自己做一些工作。” 与会者不是简单地听取演讲,而是通过祷告、赠送、短期访问、传教士评估和长期照料等实际问题开展工作。 Wooten说,教会总是告诉他最大的好处是清晰. 他说,“他们感谢对派遣教会的咨监委的澄清,以及我们的作用和责任。” 对于IMB的传教士彼得和凯蒂·威克斯来说,这种清晰度特别有价值. 他们与教会领袖一起参加了实验室. 他们的真名被更改以保护自己在东南亚的工作. 彼得说,“在这几天里,我宁愿呆在这里。” 凯蒂对培训的互动性表示赞赏. 我非常欣赏他们要求不同教会提供信息的方式, 从传教士的角度来看,她认为实验室解决了共同的挑战. title_zh: 数字化之门为东南亚岛民打开福音之门
content: Just as young people today have become more comfortable with talking online than in person, the same is true for people in Southeast Asia. IMB missionaries are creating and publishing Jesus-focused ads, videos and other digital content to connect with the lost through the internet. IMB Photo Recently, an International Mission Board team in Southeast Asia asked a young woman if she had heard the story of Jesus. She replied that, yes, she had heard about Him through a video online! “Back in the day,” shared Amanda Clarkston, an IMB missionary who has served in Southeast Asia for 33 years, “when I first came on the field, you’d go somewhere and gather all the people together in the village to watch the JESUS film.” Now, face-to-face conversations about Christ on the Southeast Asian islands are harder to accomplish. While teams travel to these remote islands often, living in a sparsely populated, animistic background culture as a foreigner creates suspicion and make long-term ministry difficult. Furthermore, young people today have become more comfortable with talking online than they are in person, Clarkston said, which is true of the islanders as well. Attempting to have a spiritual conversation face-to-face has become “too much” for locals, Clarkston shared. So, how do you share the gospel with multiple people groups who are constantly online and less comfortable with in-person interactions? For these Southeast Asia teams, digital engagement — the use of social media platforms to share a message — has become a plausible and effective entry point. The social media agency We Are Social confirmed this, revealing that 82.4% of Southeast Asia’s population uses the internet. “No matter where they go, how far they go, how remote it is, people have phones,” Clarkston and her team realized, “And though sometimes they do have to climb up the highest peak to get reception, people do it.” Clarkston’s team has begun creating and publishing Jesus-focused ads, videos and other digital content in hopes of building bridges to the islanders through the internet. Viewers can click on the ad to message back and forth with a responder, a local believer or missionary who is available to pray, build relationships and answer spiritual questions. “It seems like locals are more open to watching those things in the privacy of their own cell phones,” Clarkston said. Clarkston intends to use digital engagement as a means for initial contact with people with animistic backgrounds, evangelism and, eventually, discipleship. She said that this new ministry has the potential to open doors with individuals across these islands who would normally never reach out on their own or respond to the gospel in person. “Maybe they’ll respond this way,” Clarkston said, “I know without a shadow of a doubt that God is calling people to Himself.” Now, more than ever, technology has a grip on society. Many spend hours each day mindlessly scrolling, searching for meaning, for happiness. And now, more than ever, there is an incredible opportunity to plant seeds across Southeast Asian islands through digital engagement. The IMB Southeast Asia team gives praise to the Lord that He has provided a creative way to reach the lost and plant seeds. Pray the people among the Southeast Asian islands would see these ads and engage with responders boldly, even though they may face persecution or harm because of it. Names were changed for security. Mikah Young is serving overseas with the IMB. The work of the IMB is sustained through faithful giving to the Cooperative Program and the Lottie Moon Christmas Offering ® . Clarkston说, “当地人似乎更愿意在手机的隐私中观看这些东西。 克拉克斯顿打算用数字化的接战作为与有动画背景,福音派,并最终有门徒身份的人进行初步接触的手段. 她说,这个新的部有可能对这些岛屿上的个人敞开大门,他们通常不会独自伸出援手或亲自回应福音。 “也许他们会以这种方式回应,”克拉克斯顿说,“我毫不怀疑地知道,上帝正在号召人们投靠自己。 ” 现在,技术比以往更加控制社会。 许多人每天花上数小时无所顾忌地滚动,寻找意义,追求幸福. 现在,比以往任何时候,通过数字化参与,在东南亚各岛屿播种种子的机会比以往任何时候都多。 IMB东南亚队称赞了"主",他为到达失落地并播下种子提供了创造性的方法. 请东南亚各岛屿人民看到这些广告,并大胆地与回应者接触,尽管他们可能因此而面临迫害或伤害。 更改了安全名称。 米卡·杨在IMB海外服役. title_zh: IMB传教士在服务之旅中分享首尔的愿景
content: Ask most people what comes to mind when they think of South Korea, and they’ll likely mention K-pop, skincare, cutting-edge technology, or bustling city streets filled with young professionals. Hun and Eunjoo Sol see those things too. But after more than a decade serving as International Mission Board missionaries in Seoul, they also see something many visitors never notice. “Many people think that Korea is exciting and successful,” Hun said. “They think about the K-pop, the K-culture, K-technology, K-cosmetics. Yes, good things… But many Korean people are struggling right now.” The Sols, who were featured in the 2025 Week of Prayer for International Missions , continue to rely on the prayers of faithful Southern Baptists. Prayers sustain them and help to push back the darkness they confront in their home culture. Hun often describes that hidden struggle with a Korean word: han. There is no simple English translation. It speaks to a deep sorrow shaped by generations of war, division, loss, and the quiet resolve to endure. Hun sees it in the young adults he meets every week—people navigating loneliness and relentless expectations, quietly asking what their lives are for beneath a veneer of success. Han is heavy. For many young adults, that weight can feel unbearable. Suicide is one of the leading causes of death among teenagers and young adults in South Korean. Hun and Eunjoo see the effects of that reality every day, and it’s one reason they believe they have no time to waste. That understanding shaped the week of Serve Tour Seoul this summer. There were no construction sites, no paintbrushes, no tools or work gloves. Instead, the team stepped into ministries local churches had been faithfully building long before the volunteers arrived. In May, 27 volunteers from seven churches across the United States came alongside local churches already serving their communities in Seoul, Paju, and Gwangju. They taught English classes, ran children’s camps, walked neighborhoods in prayer, distributed food, and sat down with college students, one conversation at a time. For Nick Holst of Sandals Church in Riverside, California, the goal was simple enough to say in a sentence: “We came to meet people,” Holst said. “We want to hear their stories, and that leads to some very meaningful connections as you get past the surface into something deeper.” That’s where the week actually lived: past the surface and past the small talk, where the quiet weight of han is often carried without words. On college campuses, volunteers played games, asked questions and mostly just listened. Some conversations lasted a few minutes and ended there. Others kept going long past the point where either person expected them to. One morning, after asking his church back home to pray, Holst sat down with a university student named Intec. They talked about culture first, the way strangers do, and then the conversation turned somewhere neither of them planned. “I got to ask him, ‘What do Koreans believe?’” Holst recalled. Intec said he didn’t believe in God. Then he recited John 3:16 from memory, word for word, a verse he’d heard somewhere along the way and never forgotten. Before they parted, Holst asked if he could pray that God would keep drawing Intec toward Himself. “He said yes.” In a city where many conversations never move beyond the surface, the exchange was a reminder of why the team had come. Not to win an argument, but to listen, to ask questions, and to trust God with what happens next. The same pattern unfolded elsewhere, beginning in classrooms and ending on city streets. Jeremy Doyle, missions pastor at Valley Baptist Church in Bakersfield, California, watched an English conversation club grow from two students on its first night to eight by the second. Nobody advertised it as anything more than a place to practice English, but the room kept filling, and so did the conversations. The team’s work with students didn’t stop there. content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I like to let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. It is a quieter week than the last one, but it brings a revised edition of B. B. Warfield’s Biblical and Theological Studies, Alex Duke’s guided tour of Exodus (for which I provided a foreword), and two Crossway editions marking 500 years since William Tyndale’s English New Testament. On the academic side, you’ll find several noteworthy titles, including the New International Commentary on the Old Testament volume on Daniel 7–12. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. Books for Everyone Zondervan From Silence to Sinai A Guided Tour of Exodus Alex Duke Publisher’s description What adjectives would you use to describe the Bible? Inspired. Amazing. Unique. Authoritative. Perfect. Pure. Life-changing. Those descriptions are all deserved. Your pastors and parents and Sunday School teachers were right. There’s no book like God’s Book. Here’s another adjective: confusing. The Bible can be confusing, especially certain parts of the Old Testament. Moments after coming across something inspiring and encouraging, you’ll read something that makes you wonder, What is even happening right now!? The book of Exodus is no exception. This sequel to Genesis begins with God’s surprising silence. What a stark contrast to Genesis, where God’s words set everything in motion. It then tells the story of God’s miraculous liberation of his people, complete with frogs falling from the sky and life-saving blood being painted over doorways. Finally, for the last half of the book, the action slows down as the people of God gather at the mountain of God to receive the Law of God in order to engage in the worship of God. From silence to Sinai, that’s the story of Exodus. To understand it all, most of us will need a guide. We’ll need some help. That’s what From Silence to Sinai is for. Alex Duke walks readers through the book of Exodus to show that nothing in God’s story is wasted—not the silence, not the ten signs, and not even the confusing parts. In Exodus, God is not absent, random, or unclear. He is revealing himself, redeeming his people, and teaching them how to live in his presence. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . content: Let me take a moment to remind you of some of the features of this site you may not know about. I have a growing page of Liturgies meant to help the local church in its worship. I also offer Book Recommendations across many categories and a list of the Best Commentaries for each book of the Bible. And if you like the quote graphics I share day by day, you can find them all at SquareQuotes.church where they are free to download. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several of the “Heart Talks” mini books that are meant to help women with common concerns: feeling like failures in parenting, husbands who lead poorly, doubt, and so on. You’ll also find Greg Gifford’s Lies My Therapist Told Me and several other titles. Recommended Reading Beer, Beef and Player’s Navy Cut. This is a brilliant article about C.S. Lewis and the vices that dogged him throughout his life—a three-pack-a day smoking habit, eating habits that bordered on gluttony, and far more alcohol than anyone should consume. “In case you really are new here and you mostly know Lewis from the kid’s books, let’s state the obvious: the man we universally honor as one of the 20th Century’s great saints smoked, ate and drank like he was a sponsored athlete of consumption. He sinned frequently through overindulgence. What do we do with this information?” How to Graciously Say No. You have probably run into the same conclusion I have: it’s often far harder to say no than to say yes. Yet sometimes the best thing we can do for ourselves and for others is to say no. Reagan Rose offers some thoughts on that (for those who have the ability to say no, of course, since in many occupations saying no isn’t an option). Can’t You Let Me Just Attend? “We live in a chronically noncommittal society. No wonder, then, that this has been dubbed the age of anxiety. Surely, covenant relationships aren’t the only cure, but it might surprise us how much stability of soul comes from deep, reliable, unflighty fellowship.” David Mathis explains why commitment to a particular church is so important, even if it’s extremely countercultural. When Morningness Is Confused With Godliness. I always enjoy an article that provides an alternate view of something we almost take for granted. That’s the case with this one from Cole Mizel, who is concerned that we may be too quick to imply that the best Christians do their daily devotions in the morning. “But is it really more virtuous to be a morning person than a night owl?” Everyone Doesn’t React the Same Way. J.V. Fesko makes a simple but wise point here: everyone doesn’t respond to preaching the same way. Because that’s the case, we should not assume that those who display a lot of emotion are necessarily being impacted more than those who do not. “Tears are not the sacrament of a changed heart, the visible sign and seal of an anguished and healed soul.” Evangelising With a Dog. I enjoyed reading Peter Barnes’s account of evangelizing with a dog. “My doctor, who is half my size, suggested as tactfully as he could, what was obvious to all – that my squash days were over, and that I should take to walking the dog in the morning and at lunchtime. content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Moody Publishers and adapted from The Unstoppable Gospel by Karl Clauson. It’s impossible to disciple lost people. That sounds obvious. Maybe too obvious to even say out loud. But when the church dilutes or neglects the good news, devastation is left in its wake. After forty years of ministry, this is the most sobering truth I’ve learned about the Western church: We do not merely have a discipleship problem today. We have a gospel problem. Before we ever became weak at disciple-making, we began redefining conversion itself. We slowly traded supernatural regeneration for human decision. Salvation became a prayer to repeat, a card to sign, an aisle to walk, while millions were assured of heaven without ever being transformed by the power of God. We didn’t offer them a belief lacking power, we offered them a powerless belief. The result is a generation that has been deeply Christianized but not necessarily changed. They know the language. They know the songs. They know when to stand, when to sit, when to say amen. They have been immersed in church culture, yet many have never been brought from death to life. We have filled churches with people who have learned how to function in and around “Christianity” without ever truly following Christ. And when that happens, discipleship collapses under the weight of human effort. When evangelism centers on human decision, discipleship inevitably becomes self-powered. Following Jesus is reduced to behavior management, moral striving, and “try harder next time.” The supernatural life Christ promised is replaced with self-help dressed up in religious garb. Dallas Willard spoke of “the Great Omission,” the church’s failure to make disciples. He was right. But I believe something even deeper has happened. Before we omitted discipleship, we compromised the very gospel that births disciples in the first place. That is the crisis. That is the great deception. And until we recover the true faith that changes everything, we will continue trying to disciple people who have never truly been made alive. We have, sitting in our church chairs and pews every weekend—even in good, Bible-teaching churches—vast numbers of people who believe themselves to be saved but possess no power beyond their own efforts and whose lives show only surface evidence of new birth. People assume what they have is all God has for them, not knowing they are cultural Christians, so close yet so far from God. People who have been taught a version of Christianity divorced from repentance, from surrender, from the cost of discipleship and, tragically, from the power that makes the gospel unstoppable. Many profess Christ but don’t possess Christ. We’ve left people needing more, wanting more, and settling for too little. The great deception must end. There is life for the spiritually dead. There is surrender that leads to life instead of loss. There is repentance that produces the rhythm of a flourishing soul. There is discipline that flows from grace instead of fear or performance. And there is deep, liberating, unmistakable freedom when Christ becomes everything. This is why truth must be championed. Not as an idea, but as a reality that cuts, clarifies, and calls us forward. Because when truth becomes really clear, it doesn’t just inform you. It changes you. It brings you out of the fog, out of the confusion, out of the illusion—and into a life that is grounded, whole, and fully alive with God. This is the gospel that birthed the early church. This is the gospel that turned the world upside down. This is the gospel that sustains God’s kids under brutal persecution today. This is the gospel the church has forgotten and the good news it desperately needs. This is the gospel that still changes everything today. Learn more about how we’ve embraced a version of the gospel that falls short of the life Jesus promised, and how you can go from powerless belief to a true faith that changes everything. Get

博客由Mody出版社赞助, 门徒不可能失去人 这听起来很明显。 也许太明显了,甚至不能大声说出来。 但当教堂淡化或忽略了好消息时,毁灭就留在了它的后面.

这是40年的牧师, 我们今天不只是有门徒问题。 我们有一个福音问题。 在做门徒之前,我们开始重新定义皈依本身。 我们慢慢地用超自然再生来换取人类的决定。

救世主成为了重复的祷告,签字的名片,行走的走道,而数百万人则得到天堂的保证,永远没有被上帝的力量所改变. 我们并没有给他们一个没有权力的信仰, 其结果是一代人被深深地基督教化,但不一定改变. 他们知道语言。 他们知道歌曲。

他们知道何时可以站起,何时可以坐起,何时可以说阿门. 他们被浸入了教会文化中,然而许多人从未被从死亡中带入生命. 我们向教会灌输了那些学会如何在 " 基督教 " 内和周围运作而不真正遵循基督的人。 当这种情况发生时,门徒们在人类努力的重压下崩溃了.

当福音会以人类的决定为中心时,门徒不可避免地会变得自强自强. 追随耶稣被贬为行为管理、道德努力和“下次更努力”的人。 基督所承诺的超自然生命被取而代之的是身穿宗教外衣的自救. Dallas Willard谈到了教会未能培养出门徒的“大意念”。 他说得对。

但我相信发生了更深层的事 在我们忽略了门徒身份之前,我们破坏了出生的门徒们最初的福音。 这就是危机。 这是伟大的欺骗。 直到我们恢复改变一切的真正信仰之前,我们将继续尝试向从未真正被活生生地培养出来的门徒.

我们每个周末都坐在教堂的椅子上和教堂的树上,即使是好的,也是圣经教学的教堂。 我们有许多人相信自己是被拯救的,但除了自己的努力之外没有权力,他们的生活只显示新出生的表面证据。 人们猜想自己拥有的只是上帝给他们的一切,他们不知道自己是文化上的基督徒,所以距离上帝还相去甚远.

曾被教过基督教的人脱离了忏悔、投降、门徒费用以及可悲的使福音无法被阻止的力量。 许多人信奉基督, 我们让人们需要更多,需要更多, 伟大的欺骗必须结束。 精神上死去的人有生命

投降导致生命而不是损失。 有悔过感产生出一个繁荣的灵魂的节奏. 纪律是从优雅而不是恐惧或表现中产生的。 当基督变成一切时,有深刻的,解放的,不可磨灭的自由. 这就是为什么必须捍卫真理。 不是作为一个想法,而是作为一个现实,削减、澄清和召唤我们前进。

title: A La Carte (November 9)
summary: Christianity under the progressive gaze / Why Christians must reject the conspiratorial mind / Wise people strive to be wiser / The pro-life movement’s midterm reckoning / How evil works / Preaching in paragraphs / Kindle deals / and more. See Also A La Carte (September 10) A La Carte (February 10) A La Carte (January 15)
summary_zh: 渐进式凝视下的基督教/为什么基督徒必须拒绝阴谋的思想/明智的人努力变得更聪明/反堕胎运动的中期清算/邪恶是如何运作的/段落中的讲道/Kindle交易/等等。另请参阅单点（ 9月10日）单点（ 2月10日）单点（ 1月15日）
title_zh: 点菜（ 11月9日）
content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several excellent biographies from Crossway. Each of them is good, but I’m partial to the one on R.C. Sproul. Note that these biographies are typically priced between $22 and $40. In case you missed it on the weekend, Westminster Books is offering a deep discount on the new graphic novel adaptation of Pilgrim’s Progress . Recommended Reading Christianity Under the Progressive Gaze. Kyle Borg: “What interests me more than politics is the apparent cultural strength and growing respectability of progressive Christianity. In fact, a headline in The Guardian boldly declared: ‘A progressive understanding of Christianity won in the US elections.’ In a society where historic Christian convictions — and I don’t just mean Reformed confessionalism but basic creedal Christianity — is often treated with suspicion, if not hostility, some expressions of ‘Christianity’ seem to be enjoying a rather warm reception.” Counterfeit Providence: Why Christians Must Reject the Conspiratorial Mind. Mitchell Bahnsen explores the conspiratorial mind and explains why it’s so important for Christians to reject it. “None of this requires Christians to become gullible or naive. Psalm 2 describes kings taking counsel together against the Lord, and the crucifixion itself was a conspiracy carried out jointly by religious and governmental authorities. True connivance does occur, and wisdom to discern the truth is necessary in a complex and fallen world. However, we must defend against a totalizing hermeneutic of suspicion, lest it become its own form of faith.” Wise People Strive To Be Wiser. Justin Huffman discusses a principle that may be obvious, but is also important. “The wise person is always seeking to become wiser still. The truly spiritual person recognizes his or her constant need for spiritual growth.” The Pro-Life Movement’s Midterm Reckoning. First Things allows everyone to access several free articles per month, and this one from Jonathon Van Maren is worth one of the quota. He considers how the battle against abortion is likely to look very different after the midterm elections. “‘It’s impossible to sugarcoat it,’ Marjorie Dannenfelser of Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America wrote in a memo issued on November 3. The 2026 midterm election results ‘are a disaster for the unborn, for their mothers, and for the country as a whole. Democrats are on track to control two of the three pieces they need to legalize taxpayer-funded abortion on demand, up until birth, in all fifty states—something they promise to start pushing as soon as they take office in January.'” How Evil Works. John Piper helpfully explains how evil works. “At the center of Satan’s purpose is to deceive on earth and to accuse in heaven. If he can deceive you about God and Christ, you will perish. If he can successfully accuse you of unforgiven sin in heaven, you will perish. And Jesus calls him ‘a murderer from the beginning’ (John 8:44). So, the deception and the accusation and the eternal death that results from unforgiven sin is a way of destroying people and opposing God.” Preaching in Paragraphs. This may be helpful for preachers to read as they let last week’s sermon fade into the past and begin to think about the next one. “Every preacher knows the terror of a blank screen. It is Tuesday morning—or even worse, Saturday afternoon—and the preacher sits and stares at his laptop. He has opened a new document in his word processor, and now the cursor stands idling on the page, patiently blinking. And the words aren’t coming.” Reader Recommendations Once a week, I like to ask what you enjoy and recommend. What books, products, videos, sites, or other experiences do you recommend to others who read this blog/newsletter? Let me know, and I’ll share a collection on Saturday. (If you’re reading this via email, you’ll need to visit my site to fill out the form. Go here to read last week’s recommendations.) Submit

title: I Regret to Inform You That Heaven Tourism Is Back
summary: I regret to inform you, dear reader, that heaven tourism is back. The genre possibly never went away entirely, but it did at least disappear from the bestseller lists for several years. Sadly, it has returned in Gabe Poirot’s 18 Days in Heaven. See Also My Top Book Reviews of All-Time The Bestsellers: Heaven Is For Real Greetings From Heaven: A Modern History of Heaven Tourism
summary_zh: 亲爱的读者，很遗憾地通知您，天堂旅游又回来了。这种风格可能永远不会完全消失，但它至少在畅销书榜上消失了好几年。可悲的是，它在加布·波洛的《天堂18天》中又回来了。另请参阅我对畅销书的热门书评：天堂是真正的来自天堂的问候：天堂旅游的现代历史
title_zh: 很遗憾地通知您，天堂旅游又回来了
content: I regret to inform you, dear reader, that heaven tourism is back. The genre possibly never went away entirely, but it did at least disappear from the bestseller lists for several years. Sadly, it has returned in Gabe Poirot’s 18 Days in Heaven , which was one of the bestselling Christian books last month and even made its way to the New York Times list of bestsellers—a feat most authors can only dream of. Out of sheer magnanimity (and perhaps a morbid sense of curiosity), I read it so you don’t have to. 18 Days in Heaven Gabe Poirot Before I tell you what it’s all about, here’s a brief history of heaven tourism. Don Piper kicked off the genre in 2004 with 90 Minutes in Heaven , and it proved a surprise hit that quickly dominated the sales charts, eventually tallying upwards of 8 million copies sold. Todd Burpo’s Heaven Is for Real followed in 2010 with over 10 million copies sold. That same year brought Kevin and Alex Malarkey’s The Boy Who Came Back from Heaven , which sold more than a million copies before Alex recanted his story and the publisher pulled it. The genre went on to deliver many more heaven books and a handful of less-popular hell books like Bill Wiese’s 23 Minutes in Hell , though none ever reached the same heights as the first few—no pun intended. My contribution to the genre was little more than reviewing several of the books and coining the snarky phrase “heaven tourism,” which, much to my delight, soon caught on . The genre inevitably ran its course, but has now returned in Gabe Poirot’s 18 Days in Heaven: I Left My Body. I Met Jesus. What He Told Me Will Alter Your Eternity . Sadly, but not surprisingly, it is just as bad as its predecessors, mixing truth with errors and documented facts with spurious speculations until it is as confusing and unreliable as any of them. 18 Days in Heaven follows the standard pattern by beginning with an account of a terrible accident—in this case, a head injury that resulted from a skateboarding mishap. Poirot, a young evangelist with a sizable YouTube following, was rendered comatose and remained hovering between life and death for 18 days. But while his body was inert, his soul was transported to heaven, where it experienced heavenly wonders, not the least of which was spending time with Jesus. What did he see and experience there? Many things, of course, some of which he is able to describe and many of which he insists he cannot, either because God told him not to or because they defy description. What can he describe? Jesus’s eyes, in which “I saw all the colors that had ever existed or could exist, all in one. He was the deepest ocean of liquid love that had no end. A spectrum of intensity that only increased the longer I stared. His eyebrows, hair, jawline, arms, chest, heart, stature, ears, forehead, eyelashes, teeth, mouth, skin, and complexion all said the same thing: I love you, I love you, I love you.” He describes Jesus’s scars which “were like an ocean that had no floor,” and had the name “Gabriel” written immediately above them. He learned from them that Jesus has completely and eternally forgotten his sins so that he could no longer remember them even if he wanted to. He smelled Jesus and observed that his “fragrance wasn’t like the humidity of the Florida Everglades. No, this was something eternal—an everlasting fountain of fire, not just surrounding me but burning into me. Wrapping around me like a robe, like a living garment of pure, unending presence. It felt burning hot and freezing cold at the same time.” He heard Jesus say many words and noted that his “words were not just a separate entity that He ‘released.’ They were like the sharpest spears that went right into the core of my very being. But these spears were not separate from Him—they were Him.” Poirot even saw his own conception: “The light from Father God united with the earthly seed from my father and the egg of my mother in that moment, and I began my existence on earth. I was not born just on

不幸的是,它回到了Gabe Poirot的"天堂18天"中,这是上个月最畅销的基督教书籍之一,甚至走进了纽约时报畅销书榜,这是大多数作者只能梦想的功绩。 我读了这篇文章,

同年,凯文和亚历克丝·马拉克的"从天堂回来的男孩"(The Boy Who Came from Heaven)也带来了,后者在亚历克丝收回他的故事并被出版商拉出之前就售出超过一百万份. 虽然没有人能达到与前几本书相同的高度,

我对这个流派的贡献不过是回顾几本书, 但现在又回到了Gabe Poirot在天堂的18天:我离开了我的身体。 我遇见了耶稣。 他告诉我 Will 改变你的永恒

Poirot是一位年轻的福音传播者,他带着一个庞大的YouTube跟随,因此被昏迷并徘徊在生与死之间长达18天. 但虽然他的身体是惰性的,他的灵魂被运到了天堂,在那里它经历了天堂的奇事,其中最起碼是和耶稣一起度过. 他在那里看到了什么? 体验什么?

当然,许多事情,有些是他能够描述的,有些是他坚持不能描述的,要么是因为上帝告诉他不要描述,要么是因为他们藐视描述。 他能描述什么? 耶稣的眼睛,其中,“我看到了曾经存在或可能存在的所有颜色,都是一种颜色。 他是无尽的液体爱最深的海洋

强度的光谱 只会增加我恒星的长度 他的眉毛、发型、下巴、手臂、胸部、心、身高、耳朵、额头、睫毛、牙齿、口腔、皮肤和相貌都说了同样的话:我爱你,我爱你,我爱你。” 他描述了耶稣的伤疤,这些伤疤 " 像一片没有地的海洋 " ,上面写有 " Gabriel " 的名字。

他从他们那里得知,耶稣已经彻底地,永远地忘记了自己的罪过,这样即使他愿意也再也记不住了. 他闻到耶稣的气味并观察到他的"香气不像佛罗里达埃弗格拉德河的湿润. 不,这是永恒的东西, 一个永恒的火焰喷泉, 不仅包围着我,而且燃烧在我身上。

缠绕我就像长袍一样 像纯洁无尽的活衣 它同时感到被烧得发热而冷冻。” 他听到耶稣说出许多话,并指出他的"词不仅是一个他‘释放'的独立实体. 他们就像最锋利的长矛 直入我生命的核心

这些长矛,不是与他分开的,他们确是他。 波洛甚至看到了自己的构想:“神父所赐的光与我父亲所赐的地上种子和母亲的卵合而为一,我开始了我在地上的存在。 我不是刚出生

title: León XIV a la juventud argentina : Déjense transformar por Cristo
summary: Ante 1.200.000 personas en Palermo, el Papa los convocó a vivir la fe sin miedo, comenzar de nuevo y llevar el Evangelio a las periferias. "Todos hacia Cristo, todos con Cristo, todos como Cristo". "T
content: Ante 1.200.000 personas en Palermo, el Papa los convocó a vivir la fe sin miedo, comenzar de nuevo y llevar el Evangelio a las periferias. "Todos hacia Cristo, todos con Cristo, todos como Cristo". "Todos hacia Cristo, todos con Cristo, todos como Cristo". Con esta convocatoria, León XIV invitó a 1.200.000 jóvenes reunidos en el Monumento de los Españoles, en el barrio porteño de Palermo, a dejarse transformar por Jesús y hacer de sus vidas un testimonio de amor y misericordia. "¡Déjense transformar por Cristo! No tengan miedo de acercarse al sacramento de la Reconciliación", les pidió durante un encuentro marcado por la emoción, la alegría y la esperanza, en el que también escuchó historias de recuperación de las adicciones, discernimiento vocacional y compromiso con los más necesitados. La multitud llegó desde distintos puntos del país para participar del encuentro, que incluyó presentaciones musicales, momentos de oración y un recorrido del pontífice en papamóvil por la Avenida del Libertador. Antes de su discurso, cuatro jóvenes compartieron sus experiencias y otros dos plantearon preguntas sobre las dificultades del servicio a los más vulnerables y la integración de la fe con el trabajo y la vida cotidiana. Una Iglesia donde todos tienen lugar León XIV retomó las palabras de Francisco durante la Jornada Mundial de la Juventud de Lisboa, en 2023, cuando el Papa argentino insistió en que en la Iglesia hay lugar para "todos, todos, todos". A partir de aquella expresión, desarrolló tres dimensiones de la vida cristiana: "Todos hacia Cristo, todos con Cristo, todos como Cristo". El pontífice se dirigió especialmente a quienes crecieron lejos de la fe, dejaron de rezar, se alejaron de la Iglesia o fueron heridos por personas que debían acompañarlos. "A cada uno quisiera decirle: ¡Hay un lugar para ti en la Iglesia! Con tus preguntas, tus heridas y tu historia. Esta es también tu casa", afirmó. Y agregó: "No tienes que fingir que todo está bien ni esperar a tener la vida resuelta para acercarte". Para explicar esa posibilidad de comenzar de nuevo, recordó el encuentro de Jesús con Zaqueo y retomó una pregunta que había cambiado la historia vocacional de Guadalupe, una de las jóvenes que dio su testimonio: "¿Quién te dijo que ya es tarde?". "Nadie ha caído tan bajo que Cristo no pueda levantarlo", aseguró, al pedir comunidades cristianas con las puertas abiertas, capaces de recibir, auxiliar y acompañar. Permanecer de pie ante los ídolos de nuestro tiempo A partir del relato bíblico de los tres jóvenes que se negaron a adorar la estatua de oro del rey Nabucodonosor, León XIV advirtió sobre las falsas promesas que pueden condicionar la vida de las nuevas generaciones. "También hoy se levantan ídolos que reclaman nuestra adoración: el éxito a cualquier precio, el dinero, la obsesión por la apariencia, la popularidad o la búsqueda desenfrenada del placer", señaló. También cuestionó las formas de sometimiento vinculadas con las redes sociales y los negocios que lucran con la pornografía y las sustancias adictivas. "Hay también quienes hacen negocio ofreciendo placeres que terminan por esclavizarnos", afirmó. Frente a esas situaciones, exhortó: "¡No se arrodillen ante aquello que no puede darles vida! Y si alguna vez han caído, ¡levántense! No permitan que nada ni nadie les arrebate la libertad que Dios les ha dado". Historias que hablan de volver a empezar Uno de los testimonios que conmovió al Papa fue el de Cristian, de 25 años, quien relató su recuperación de las adicciones después de haber vivido en la calle. La Familia Grande del Hogar de Cristo lo recibió sin preguntarle por su pasado y le permitió comenzar de nuevo. "Yo estaba en la calle y el piso de la calle es duro y frío. Soy como muchos que sufren el problema de las adicciones. La droga me aisló de mi familia", contó. Hoy acompaña a otros jóvenes que atraviesan situaciones similares. También habló Guadalupe, postulante de una congregación religiosa, quien explicó que dura

title: Adicciones , vocación y solidaridad : los testimonios que escuchó León XIV en Palermo - Un joven que logró salir de las adicciones , una docente comprometida con niños vulnerables , una correntina que busca consagrar su vida a Dios y un periodista de...
summary: La vigilia juvenil que encabezó el papa León XIV en el Monumento de los Españoles, en el barrio porteño de Palermo, tuvo momentos de profunda emoción. Cuatro jóvenes subieron al escenario para contar
content: La vigilia juvenil que encabezó el papa León XIV en el Monumento de los Españoles, en el barrio porteño de Palermo, tuvo momentos de profunda emoción. Cuatro jóvenes subieron al escenario para contar sus historias, poner en palabras las dificultades que atravesaron y explicar cómo la fe transformó sus vidas. Cristian, Agustina, Guadalupe y Franco llegaron desde distintas realidades, pero coincidieron en un mismo mensaje: la posibilidad de encontrar un nuevo camino a partir del acompañamiento, el compromiso con los demás y la confianza en Dios. También te puede interesar: Sus testimonios permitieron acercar al Santo Padre las inquietudes de una generación que enfrenta desafíos sociales, personales y espirituales. Cristian: de vivir en la calle a encontrar una oportunidad para empezar de nuevo Uno de los relatos más conmovedores fue el de Cristian, quien habló abiertamente sobre su lucha contra las adicciones y las consecuencias que el consumo problemático tuvo en su vida. El joven recordó que llegó a alejarse de sus seres queridos y terminó viviendo en la calle, en una situación en la que su principal preocupación era conseguir drogas. "Mi prioridad era el consumo. La droga me aisló de mi familia", contó frente a León XIV. Su recuperación comenzó cuando encontró refugio en el Hogar de Cristo de Moreno Sur, donde recibió contención, alimento y un lugar donde dormir. Allí, según relató, pudo recuperar la esperanza y comenzar a reconstruir su vida. "Hoy estoy de pie gracias a la familia grande del Hogar de Cristo, de Moreno Sur, que un día me recibió sin preguntarme quién era, me dio un abrazo y me invitó un plato de comida caliente y una cama para dormir. Yo estaba en la calle", expresó. Cristian también destacó la importancia de la espiritualidad para afrontar los momentos más difíciles de su recuperación: "Cuando me siento desbordado escucho a Jesús y la paz vuelve". Agustina: dejó Buenos Aires para acompañar a chicos en Viedma La historia de Agustina estuvo marcada por su vocación de servicio. Nacida en Buenos Aires, es maestra de nivel primario y desde los 16 años participa en iniciativas de voluntariado y apoyo escolar. Hace un año tomó una decisión importante: trasladarse a Viedma, Río Negro, para continuar trabajando con niños que atraviesan situaciones de vulnerabilidad. Durante su testimonio, explicó que acompañar a quienes más lo necesitan también implica enfrentarse a situaciones que exceden las posibilidades de cualquier persona. La frustración aparece cuando, a pesar del esfuerzo y la dedicación, no siempre se consiguen los resultados esperados. Por eso, aprovechó el encuentro para plantearle una inquietud al Papa: "Santo Padre, ¿cómo afrontar la frustración y nuestros límites cuando no logramos acompañar a los excluidos como quisiéramos? ¿Cómo seguir caminando junto a ellos cuando sentimos que lo que hacemos no alcanza?". Su pregunta abrió un espacio de reflexión sobre la importancia de perseverar en las tareas solidarias, incluso cuando los frutos del trabajo no se manifiestan de inmediato. Guadalupe: una joven correntina que busca consagrar su vida a Dios Desde Corrientes llegó Guadalupe, quien atraviesa una etapa de formación para ingresar a la congregación de las Hermanas de la Presentación de la Virgen María de Granada. Frente a León XIV, recordó la influencia que tuvo su familia en la construcción de su fe. Sus padres le enseñaron desde pequeña que las capacidades y oportunidades que recibe cada persona deben ponerse al servicio de los demás. "Mis padres me enseñaron que los dones que cada uno tiene no se deben guardar, sino dar a los demás", relató. Sin embargo, también reconoció que el camino de discernimiento de su vocación estuvo acompañado por dudas y momentos de incertidumbre. En particular, habló del peso que pueden tener las opiniones ajenas al momento de tomar decisiones personales. "Empezaron a pesar en mí las palabras de los demás", recordó, al compartir las dificultades que debió afrontar mientras

title: Papa León XIV pide renovar la vocación religiosa en Argentin | DIARIO DEL SUR
summary: El papa León XIV hizo un llamado a renovar el compromiso de la vida religiosa y fortalecer la labor evangelizadora de la Iglesia durante un encuentro con obispos, sacerdotes, diáconos, religiosos, rel
content: El papa León XIV hizo un llamado a renovar el compromiso de la vida religiosa y fortalecer la labor evangelizadora de la Iglesia durante un encuentro con obispos, sacerdotes, diáconos, religiosos, religiosas, seminaristas y agentes pastorales en la Catedral de Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, en Córdoba, Argentina. La reunión se realizó durante el tercer día de su viaje apostólico por el país sudamericano. En su intervención, el pontífice invitó a los representantes de la Iglesia a mantener viva la vocación, recuperar el entusiasmo de los primeros años de servicio y trabajar por comunidades más abiertas, solidarias y comprometidas con las necesidades de la población. Bajo el mensaje de “¡Sueñen con una Iglesia que siga haciendo lío!”, León XIV destacó que el testimonio cristiano no depende únicamente de las palabras o de las actividades religiosas, sino también de la manera en que cada persona vive su vocación y se relaciona con los demás. Recuperar el sentido de la vocación Durante su discurso, el Papa recordó que toda vocación nace de una llamada y de una decisión personal de seguir a Cristo. Señaló que, con el paso de los años, las responsabilidades, las obligaciones y el cansancio pueden hacer que algunos religiosos pierdan de vista el motivo que los llevó a dedicar su vida al servicio de la Iglesia. Por esta razón, invitó a los presentes a reflexionar sobre su relación con Dios y a evitar que la rutina, las rivalidades o la comodidad debiliten su compromiso. También destacó la importancia de mantener espacios de oración, revisar las propias acciones y reconocer los errores como parte del camino de crecimiento espiritual. El pontífice advirtió sobre el riesgo de trabajar constantemente para la Iglesia y dedicar cada vez menos tiempo a fortalecer la vida espiritual. Según expresó, la vocación necesita conservar el fuego que la impulsó desde el comienzo. Recordó a figuras religiosas de Argentina León XIV también hizo referencia a personajes que han marcado la historia religiosa del país, entre ellos Mama Antula, el santo Cura Brochero y el beato Ceferino Namuncurá. Sobre Mama Antula, destacó su esfuerzo por llevar los Ejercicios Espirituales a diferentes comunidades, recorriendo largas distancias para acercar a las personas a la fe. También recordó al Cura Brochero, quien desarrolló su labor pastoral en las sierras argentinas y continuó acompañando a su pueblo incluso durante sus años de enfermedad. El Papa mencionó además al beato Ceferino Namuncurá, cuya vida, aunque breve, dejó un testimonio de compromiso religioso. Estas figuras fueron presentadas como ejemplos de entrega, perseverancia y servicio a las comunidades. Una Iglesia que responda a las necesidades sociales Otro de los puntos centrales del encuentro fue la responsabilidad de la Iglesia frente a las dificultades que atraviesan las comunidades. El pontífice señaló que situaciones como la pobreza, la enfermedad, la soledad, el desempleo y la falta de vivienda digna requieren respuestas concretas. En ese sentido, pidió a los sacerdotes y agentes pastorales mantener una actitud de cercanía con las personas que necesitan acompañamiento, sin limitar su misión a las actividades tradicionales de las instituciones religiosas. También animó a los seminaristas y jóvenes que se preparan para la vida consagrada a mirar la realidad desde una perspectiva de servicio, reconociendo las necesidades de la población y estando dispuestos a asumir responsabilidades que quizá no habían imaginado inicialmente. Creatividad para llevar el mensaje a nuevas generaciones León XIV destacó la importancia de encontrar nuevas formas de transmitir el mensaje cristiano, especialmente en una sociedad donde las herramientas digitales y las transformaciones culturales modifican las maneras de comunicarse. title: León XVI celebró misa en Córdoba y apuntó : Estamos llamados a la santidad – 4SEMANAS | Últimas noticias de Argentina y el mundo
summary: El papa León XIV encabezó este martes su segunda multitudinaria misa en el país en la Escuela de Aviación Militar de Córdoba, donde pronunció una sentida homilía centrada en la rica tradición de santi
content: El papa León XIV encabezó este martes su segunda multitudinaria misa en el país en la Escuela de Aviación Militar de Córdoba, donde pronunció una sentida homilía centrada en la rica tradición de santidad de la región y en el compromiso evangelizador de los fieles. Durante la ceremonia celebrada ante una multitud en el Polo Aeronáutico cordobés, el Sumo Pontífice destacó que la región “ha sido rica en frutos de santidad” y recordó que por sus calles transitaron personas que dieron la vida por el Evangelio, mencionando especialmente al cura Brochero y a Mama Antula. Además, nombró a todos los santos y beatos de la Argentina, en una homilía centrada estrictamente en lo religoso. “Todos somos simples servidores y tenemos que cumplir con la misión que el Señor nos encomienda; estamos todos llamados a la santidad”, afirmó León XIV. En esa línea, pidió tener presente que, habiendo sido arrancado del poder de las tinieblas, el creyente ha sido trasladado «a la luz de Dios». Ante los miles de peregrinos reunidos, el Pontífice advirtió: «El mundo espera de nosotros un compromiso de vida y un testimonio de oración». «Celebramos esta misa por la santificación del pueblo argentino», resaltó el Pontífice, que agregó: «Le pido a Dios, a través de san León Magno, que nos continúe bendiciendo y nos de la gracia de confesar siempre». Y afirmó: «Vayan y sean santos, abran sus corazones». A continuación, la homilía completa del papa León XIV en Córdoba: La confesión de Pedro, que a lo largo de la historia resuena en sus sucesores, nos manifiesta el misterio de Dios revelado en Cristo para nuestra salvación. Un mensaje de salvación que sigue siendo actual y que se apoya en la intercesión de tantos hermanos nuestros en la fe, que ahora nos acompañan desde el cielo. No en vano, la tierra que ahora nos acoge ha sido rica en frutos de santidad; el ejemplo de quienes nos han precedido en este camino nos sigue interpelando a vivir como ellos vivieron y a entregar la vida, como Cristo ha hecho por nosotros y ellos supieron imitar con perfección. La ciudad de Córdoba, heredera natural de la primera sede episcopal erigida en Argentina, ha sido tierra de santos. Por sus conventos e iglesias, por sus calles y hospitales transitaron hombres y mujeres que, enamorados de Jesús, dieron la vida por el Evangelio. En Argentina vivieron hombres y mujeres, como el Cura Brochero y Mama Antula —por poner solo dos ejemplos—, que fueron llamados por el Señor y enviados a la misión, sin que ellos mismos fueran siquiera conscientes de lo extraordinario que su labor evangelizadora llegaría a ser; porque todos los cristianos somos simples servidores, no hemos de hacer más que cumplir con nuestro deber. Gozoso deber, pues, el de cumplir con la misión que el Señor nos encomienda a cada uno de nosotros. Sí, queridos hermanos y hermanas. Estamos todos llamados a la santidad; en eso consiste nuestra labor en la tierra, en alcanzar la perfecta unión con Dios. Una llamada que, además, siempre es misionera: tenemos que dar a conocer a los demás la belleza que nosotros hemos conocido en Cristo. Como cristianos, debemos «enseñar todo lo que es conforme a la sana doctrina». En este sentido, hago mía ahora también esta exhortación de san León Magno, cuya memoria litúrgica hoy celebramos y a cuya protección me encomiendo: «Reconoce, oh cristiano, tu dignidad, pues participas de la divina naturaleza, y no quieras volver a la antigua vileza con una vida depravada. Recuerda de qué cabeza y de qué cuerpo eres miembro. Ten presente que habiendo sido arrancado del poder de las tinieblas has sido transportado a la luz y al reino de Dios». No hay mejor modo de enseñar que dando ejemplo con la propia vida, pues «el mundo espera de nosotros un compromiso de vida y un testimonio de oración». Esto exige una adhesión total a Jesucristo, sin fisuras. Este es el testimonio de los santos y es algo que nos hace vivir con esperanza, aún en medio de la dificultad.
